items.title: Los riesgos de la IA dialógica en la educación superior: afectaciones cognitivas y en la capacidad de lecto-escritura
items.abstract: Dialogic Artificial Intelligence (DAI) or communicative AI within Large Language Models (LLMs) is rapidly expanding across higher education and academic workflows in both teaching and research. The adoption of DAI is being driven by the pressure to enhance productivity and automate academic practices. This paper discusses the primary risks that the intensive use of DAI poses to human cognitive capacities, information biases, and the erosion of literacy, critical thinking, argumentation, and academic discourse skills. Furthermore, it analyzes emerging forms of plagiarism and misconduct facilitated by DAI while reflecting on the concept of individual authorship, which has become obsolete, giving way to human-AI co-authorship. As an immersive technology that impacts human agency and autonomy, DAI could irreversibly transform cognition, literacy, the sense of authorship, and collaborative frameworks in research, teaching, and scholarly production. Finally, it concludes with a set of criteria and recommendations to guide university regulatory policies on DAI, moving beyond prohibitions, punitive measures, or ineffective appeals to individual ethics in the use of LLMs.

items.title: Mammography datasets and artificial intelligence for breast cancer detection: challenges, bias, and future directions
items.abstract: Background Breast cancer is still one of the main causes of death in women from cancer worldwide, and early detection is crucial. Mammography is the primary imaging modality for breast cancer screening and recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have significantly enhanced automated breast cancer detection. This review takes a data-centered approach, examining key characteristics of public datasets, the contributions of mammography data to AI for breast cancer detection, and the implications for clinical generalizability. This review, however, takes a data-centered approach, critically analyzing characteristics of publicly available mammography datasets, and the role of mammography data to the development, performance and clinical generalization of AI models for the detection of breast cancer. The datasets are compared on the following aspects: dataset size, quality of the annotations, imaging modality, clinical metadata, dataset accessibility and demographic diversity. Analysis reveals that the quality, diversity and representativeness of the data used are critical for the performance and generalizability of AI models, ranging from the traditional machine learning era to the current era of deep learning, transformer-based systems, multimodal learning, explainable AI and privacy-preserving learning. Conclusion The results show that, apart from the development of AI model architectures, it is a necessity to have standardized, diverse and clinically representative datasets to make further progress in AI-assisted mammography. The review emphasizes the importance of establishing a comprehensive benchmark dataset for mammography that is large and diverse to enhance reproducibility, to fairly evaluate models, and to develop strong, clinically viable AI systems for breast cancer detection.

items.title: Mechanistic Continuity and Translational Gaps in Attention-deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Pharmacotherapy: Lessons from Animal Models to Pediatric Trials
items.abstract: Translating preclinical findings into safe and effective pharmacotherapy for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remains a major challenge in pediatric neuropsychopharmacology.This review critically examines why some mechanism-based therapies translate successfully from animal models to clinical practice, whereas others fail despite promising preclinical evidence.Among available models, the spontaneously hypertensive rat (SHR) exhibits strong construct validity and domain-specific predictive validity for conserved catecholaminergic mechanisms relevant to ADHD.Across species, successful therapies generally preserve mechanistic continuity by enhancing prefrontal catecholamine signaling through dopamine transporter inhibition, norepinephrine transporter blockade, or 2A-adrenergic receptor stimulation.Accordingly, stimulants, atomoxetine, guanfacine, and viloxazine extended-release show substantial translational and clinical success.Pediatric trials support this hierarchy, with clinician-rated standardized mean differences versus placebo of approximately 1.02 for amphetamines, 0.78 for methylphenidate, and 0.56 for atomoxetine at around 12 weeks.In contrast, nicotinic and histaminergic agents and certain dopaminergic antagonist strategies have translated poorly because of inadequate target engagement, developmental pharmacokinetic differences, and pediatric safety concerns.Importantly, SHR predictive validity is domain-specific rather than syndrome-wide, as methylphenidate more consistently improves attention and impulsivity than locomotor hyperactivity.Precision medicine, pharmacogenomics, biomarker-guided target engagement, and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches may improve future drug development.Overall, current evidence supports mechanistic continuity, rather than broad behavioral similarity, as a useful framework for translating preclinical findings into effective pediatric ADHD therapies, although prospective evaluation and refinement of this framework remain necessary.

items.title: Methodological, Data-Related, and Governance Challenges
items.abstract: This chapter critically examines the methodological, data-related, and governance challenges that constrain the effective and responsible implementation of Artificial Intelligence in Sports Science. It positions these limitations as a necessary counterbalance to prevailing technological optimism and situates them within both practical modelling workflows and broader epistemological considerations. Building on previous chapters, the analysis emphasizes the importance of validation, robustness testing, and sensitivity analysis as essential components of reliable AI systems. The chapter identifies key barriers to implementation, including economic constraints, limited access to qualified personnel, and institutional resistance-driven by cultural skepticism toward algorithmic decision-making. It further explores the tension between underutilization and overreliance on AI, highlighting risks associated with automation bias and the erosion of human expertise. From a governance perspective, the chapter examines the need for standardization, certification, and auditability, referencing frameworks such as the EU Artificial Intelligence Act and NIST guidelines. It also addresses issues of accessibility and equity, advocating for the democratization of AI technologies through open-access tools and federated learning approaches. The chapter concludes by emphasizing sustainability, stakeholder trust, and the integration of ethical, educational, and regulatory mechanisms as prerequisites for long-term AI adoption in Sports Science.

items.title: Modeling Environments and Their Relevance for Sports Science
items.abstract: This chapter examines the role of modelling environments in Artificial Intelligence workflows within Sports Science, emphasizing that analytical outcomes are shaped not only by algorithms and data but also by the software platforms used for implementation. It conceptualizes modelling environments as cognitive interfaces that mediate between domain expertise and computational reasoning, influencing data preparation, model development, interpretation, and communication of results. The chapter introduces four widely used environments—JASP, SPSS, MATLAB, and R/RStudio—and evaluates their relevance for different stages of AI modelling. Each platform is analyzed in terms of usability, transparency, extensibility, and alignment with the competencies of Sport Science practitioners. Particular attention is given to their strengths and limitations in handling statistical modeling, Machine Learning, Time-Series Analysis, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence. In addition, the chapter highlights the importance of reproducibility through the use of external repositories and LLM-assisted programming workflows. It argues for a complementary, workflow-oriented approach in which multiple environments are combined to address complex analytical tasks. By situating modelling environments within a broader methodological framework, the chapter provides a principled foundation for selecting appropriate tools and supports the development of transparent, reproducible, and data-driven practices in sports analytics and performance modeling.

items.title: Motivation as the Engine of ESL Success: Exploring Economic, Social, and Educational Determinants of Language Learning
items.abstract: Motivation represents one of the most influential factors affecting success in learning English as a second language (ESL). Although English proficiency is increasingly associated with academic achievement, professional advancement, and global mobility, students' willingness to engage in language learning is shaped by a complex interaction of economic, psychological, pedagogical, and sociocultural influences. Guided by Self-Determination Theory and the L2 Motivational Self System, this paper examines the major factors affecting student motivation in ESL learning. The discussion is organised around four interconnected dimensions: economic and instrumental motivations, academic self-efficacy and personal growth, pedagogical environments and motivational engagement, and cultural curiosity and media exposure. The analysis suggests that students are strongly motivated by career aspirations, financial stability, academic achievement, and communicative competence. At the same time, self-confidence, reduced communication anxiety, supportive learning environments, and exposure to authentic English-language media contribute significantly to sustained motivation. The paper further argues that teacher attitudes, innovative pedagogical practices, and opportunities for meaningful communication play a central role in transforming external motivation into internal commitment to language learning. Motivation is therefore conceptualised as a dynamic process shaped by personal aspirations and environmental influences rather than a fixed individual characteristic. Future research should investigate the role of artificial intelligence-assisted learning, digital motivation, multilingual identity, and long-term motivational development among ESL learners.

items.title: Multi-objective deep deterministic policy gradient for cobot trajectory planning in automotive spot welding
items.abstract: Introduction Autonomous trajectory planning is a fundamental challenge in collaborative robotic spot welding because positioning accuracy, motion smoothness, operational safety, energy use, and production efficiency must be optimized simultaneously under industrial constraints. Methods This paper presents a Pareto-Guided Multi-Objective Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (PMO-DDPG) framework for autonomous cobot trajectory planning in automotive spot welding. The framework combines a deterministic actor with four objective-specific critics for accuracy, smoothness, safety, and productivity, together with phase-dependent preferences for the approach, alignment, welding, and retraction stages. The principal novelty is a two-level multi-objective design that preserves six normalized physical reward components, maps them to four specialized critics for phase-dependent actor updates, and uses a non-dominated policy archive for Pareto-guided selection while retaining actor-only online inference. Simulation and industrial experiments assessed convergence, trajectory quality, collision avoidance, energy consumption, cycle time, success rate, and latency. Results Relative to the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) baseline, PMO-DDPG reduced trajectory error by 66.4%, collision rate by 82.1%, energy consumption by 15.5%, cycle time by 22.0%, and inference latency by 22.7%, while increasing the success rate by 7.5 percentage points. The proposed method achieved 1.08 mm trajectory error, a 1.2% collision rate, 3.65 kJ energy consumption, a 3.87 s cycle time, a 94.6% success rate, and 21.5 ms inference time. Pareto-front analysis produced non-dominated operating points for different manufacturing priorities, and 100 industrial trials confirmed sub-millimeter positioning and repeatable vision-guided welding. Discussion Within the evaluated simulation and industrial test settings, and without a formal significance test, these descriptive results indicate that PMO-DDPG is a promising accurate, safe, and efficient trajectory-planning approach.

items.title: Multifunctional Alginate–TiO2/SiO2 Hydrogel–Ceramic Composites for Photocatalytic Soil Remediation and Impedance-Based Diagnostics: A Critical Review and Conceptual Framework
items.abstract: Soil contamination by persistent organic pollutants is a major environmental challenge, whereas conventional remediation approaches often lack effective means for continuous, in situ monitoring of treatment progress. Recent advances in multifunctional materials provide a basis for integrating pollutant degradation with non-destructive environmental monitoring. This review critically examines alginate–TiO2/SiO2 hydrogel–ceramic composites as a potential platform for integrating photocatalytic soil remediation with impedance-based monitoring. TiO2 exhibits photocatalytic activity and promotes the generation of reactive oxygen species; SiO2 contributes to adsorption, dispersion, porosity, and structural stability; while sodium alginate provides a hydrated, biodegradable matrix for particle immobilization, water retention, and mass-transport control. Particular attention is given to electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) as a non-destructive method for monitoring time-dependent physicochemical changes in soil–composite systems. This review evaluates suitable composite architectures, electrode configurations, calibration strategies, control experiments, and approaches for interpreting complex impedance responses. The potential application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning is also considered, with emphasis on data quality, independent validation, and the limitations of models trained on heterogeneous environmental datasets. Because impedance responses are inherently indirect and non-specific, chemical analysis remains essential for confirming pollutant transformation and identifying transformation products. Standardized ecotoxicological assays, particularly reproduction testing with the springtail Folsomia candida, are considered as an independent biological line of evidence for determining whether physicochemical improvements are accompanied by reduced residual toxicity. Key challenges include heterogeneous soil properties, limited light penetration, mass-transfer limitations, catalyst and hydrogel stability, sensor calibration, matrix effects, and model accuracy. The review proposes an evidence-based framework linking material design, photocatalytic treatment, EIS monitoring, chemical verification, and ecotoxicological assessment. However, the complete integrated platform has not yet been experimentally validated, and its performance in real contaminated soils remains to be established.

items.title: Multimodal artificial intelligence for vascular aging: toward proactive detection and management
items.abstract: Vascular aging is a fundamental driver of cardiovascular diseases (CVD), yet identifying individuals undergoing accelerated vascular aging - and therefore at elevated cardiovascular risk - remains a significant clinical challenge. The traditional “one-size-fits-all” health risk assessments are often insensitive to early, subclinical vascular changes. The recent explosion of medical big data, coupled with the advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Multimodal Foundation Models (MFMs), offer a transformative opportunity to shift vascular aging management from reactive detection toward proactive, predictive protection. This review systematically explores the integration of multimodal artificial intelligence (MMAI) and large-scale foundation models in the identification, stratification, and personalized management of vascular aging. We first delineate the multidimensional data ecosystem of vascular aging, including electronic health records (EHRs), imaging, omics, and continuous physiological signals from wearables, and analyze how deep learning architectures enable the detection of vascular aging by capturing subclinical structural and functional alterations. We then focus on the emerging role of MFMs, which transcend task-specific AI by integrating heterogeneous data types to provide holistic phenomapping. Furthermore, we discuss the utility of Large Language Models (LLMs) in clinical workflows, enhancing patient adherence through natural language interaction, and accelerating research through knowledge synthesis. Despite the potential of foundation models, their clinical translation faces technical and institutional barriers. We analyze four systemic challenges: algorithmic fairness, regulatory uncertainty, explainable AI (XAI) and the lack of real-world validation. We propose a strategic roadmap aligned with international frameworks that progresses from standardized performance reporting for elderly subgroups in the near term to cost-effective, individualized interventions that intercept the health-to-disease transition in the long term. The convergence of big data and foundation models represents a shift from reactive cardiovascular care to proactive, precision-based longevity management, positioning early, AI-enabled identification of high-risk vascular aging phenotypes as a primary target for the next generation of preventive medicine.

items.title: Multimodal Large-Model-Driven Method for Urban 3D Green-Space Calculation and Low-Carbon Green-Space Management
items.abstract: Against the background of global carbon neutrality goals and urban ecological transformation, traditional two-dimensional green-space indicators cannot fully reflect spatial–ecological benefits, and conventional 3D green-space calculation and landscape maintenance methods suffer from low accuracy and low efficiency. This paper proposes a theoretical technical framework combining multimodal remote sensing data, LiDAR point clouds and domain large language models for urban green-space scenarios. Firstly, a multimodal feature fusion strategy is constructed to adapt to complex urban environments, and a hierarchical calculation workflow for individual trees and regional 3D green-space is designed. Secondly, a full-life-cycle carbon accounting system for landscape engineering is established, which clarifies the accounting boundaries and quantitative methods of carbon sources and carbon sinks. Thirdly, a human–computer collaborative decision framework is proposed to realise intelligent recommendations for low-carbon maintenance schemes. This study focuses on theoretical framework construction and method exploration, and verifies the technical feasibility through simulation analysis. Different from existing independent research on green-space calculation or carbon accounting, this work integrates the two tasks and innovates a multimodal model application mode for landscape industry. This study focuses on theoretical framework construction and methodological exploration; feasibility assessment is only carried out via simulation deduction, rather than real-world field validation.

items.title: Multimodal Learning for Time Series Forecasting: Architectures, Challenges, and New Directions
items.abstract: Time series forecasting increasingly exploits information that is not itself a numerical series, such as news text, imagery, contextual metadata, and relational structure among series. The term "multimodal" is nonetheless used without an operational definition, so that genuinely cross-modal models are pooled with multivariate and multi-view models that raise different problems. This paper proposes an operational criterion, together with a four-question procedure, that separates multimodal forecasting from multivariate, multi-view, and cross-modal model-reuse settings. On this basis it develops a five-axis taxonomy covering modality type, temporal alignment granularity, fusion mechanism, model family, and output form with uncertainty representation, and presents a structured synthesis of 33 published studies across eight application domains. Applying the criterion consistently shows that only 14 studies fully satisfy the definition. Notably, five large-language-model-based forecasters presented as series–text alignment methods use only text generated from the input series itself, which cannot add information about the future. Combined with published ablation evidence, this indicates that the benefit of an auxiliary modality is conditional rather than universal, and that evaluation practice, rather than architecture, is the binding constraint of the field. Generalisation under a shifting context–target relationship — the very condition auxiliary context is expected to address — remains essentially untested. The paper analyses seven groups of open challenges and proposes five research directions, notably multimodal self-supervised learning and offline semantic feature extraction with large language models, together with an eight-item minimum evaluation protocol intended to make the contribution of an auxiliary modality verifiable.

items.title: Musical Giftedness in Human-AI Creation: Interpreting Evidence Beyond the Finished Product
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence complicates a central problem in identifying musical giftedness: deciding which features of an outcome can reasonably be attributed to the student who presents it. A piece may display coherent formal design, an elaborate harmonic plan, idiomatic instrumentation, or convincing timbral balance even when those decisions were neither made nor understood by the learner. This conceptual article examines how music co-created with AI can be interpreted when the finished product no longer reveals the student’s contribution on its own. Drawing on research on musical talent development, AI-assisted creation, and assessment validity, it considers three sources of information: compositional problem framing, analytical listening and revision, and the traceability of musical decisions. Transfer across tasks provides a further check. These sources are not diagnostic criteria. They are intended to support more cautious interpretations of musical evidence in AI-mediated creative work and to complement broader developmental evidence used in identification processes.

items.title: Nanobiosensors at the Frontier: A Comprehensive Review on the Design, Digital Integration, and Clinical Applications for Next‐Generation Precision Diagnostics
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Recent progress in nanotechnology and biosensing is driving the development of advanced diagnostic tools for precision medicine. This review provides a systematic summary and critical analysis of intelligent nanobiosensors, which integrate engineered nanomaterials with biological recognition components and advanced signal‐transduction mechanisms. Key design paradigms, classification frameworks, and the role of diverse nanomaterials (e.g., metallic, carbon‐based, magnetic, and hybrid structures) are discussed in detail. Furthermore, major transduction technologies, including electrochemical, optical, mechanical, thermal, and magnetic platforms, together with clinical translation pathways and integration with artificial intelligence (AI), edge computing, and mobile health technologies, are comprehensively reviewed. Particular emphasis is placed on clinical applications in infectious, oncological, cardiovascular, and neurological diseases, as well as therapeutic monitoring. Key challenges, including scalability, data security, and regulatory barriers, are also critically discussed. Finally, emerging trends such as federated learning, the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), and personalized digital diagnostics are highlighted, providing perspectives on future directions in intelligent biosensing and precision healthcare.

items.title: Natural-language prompting builds and operates an open-source software workflow for virtual drug-discovery
items.abstract: Virtual docking and free-energy calculations can accelerate drug discovery, but practical use requires structural chemistry expertise, complex parameter selection and software integration. Here we show that iterative dialogue with an artificial intelligence (AI) coding assistant, OpenAI Codex, can guide a non-specialist scientist to build and operate a scripted, auditable computational workflow without direct coding. The assistant provided structural chemistry guidance and assembled an integrated pipeline for structure retrieval and preparation, binding-site definition, ligand preparation, virtual docking, interaction analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) and alchemical relative binding free-energy calculations. It also built a script generator for launching, monitoring and interpreting workflow runs. We tested the workflow on public cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) benchmarks. After primary docking and multi-seed hit refinement, the active-ligand fraction increased from 1.73% in the input library to 80% in the ten-candidate handoff set (46.4-fold over input); a short MD stage acted as a structural quality-control gate on the leading candidates. Docking and hit refinement also generalized to human immunodeficiency virus reverse transcriptase and kinesin family member 11 benchmarks. In a CDK2 free-energy benchmark, the workflow achieved root-mean-square error = 0.66 kcal/mol and Pearson r = 0.90. Prompt-guided AI can orchestrate computational drug-discovery workflows for non-specialists while the underlying calculations remain the work of established external software and every run remains auditable.

items.title: NEUROLEARN - A Learning Platform for Neurodiverse Students
items.abstract: Kids with autism, ADHD, or dyslexia hit roadblocks in regular schools their brains just work differently when it comes to focusing, thinking, or picking up new stuff at their own pace. That's why we built NeuroLearn AI: a web tool powered by smart tech that customizes lessons just for you, making school feel welcoming and doable. It keeps an eye on how you click, learn, and perform, then switches things up right away like easing the challenge level, changing how info shows up, or matching your best way to absorb it. You'll get helpers to stay on track, clean layouts that won't stress you out, game-like challenges to make it fun, and choices for seeing, hearing, or doing activities. All this ramps up what sticks in your head without overwhelming you, helps you learn on your own, and ditches that nagging school worry. Parents and teachers see updates as you go. Bottom line, NeuroLearn smooths out the bumps, making education fair for everyone—no matter how your mind ticks. items.title: Non-Recognition of Online Doctoral Programs in India in the Era of AI, Education 4.0, and Education 5.0: Challenges for Working Professionals
items.abstract: The expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) and digitally mediated learning has intensified debate about flexibility, access, and quality assurance in higher education. This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the non-recognition of fully online doctoral education in India, focusing on career barriers, psychological burnout, acceptance of Education 4.0, institutional resistance, and support for policy reform. Using a cross-sectional questionnaire dataset of 832 respondents, the study applies descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), group comparisons, and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression. The findings indicate comparatively high mean scores for perceived career barriers and Education 4.0 acceptance. Group comparisons did not identify statistically significant differences across the categories examined. The overall regression model was statistically significant (F(7, 824) = 64.28, p < 0.001; R² = 0.353; adjusted R² = 0.348). Institutional resistance was positively associated with policy-reform support, whereas career barriers showed a smaller negative association. Education 4.0 acceptance also showed a positive association with reform support. These findings represent statistical relationships within the sample and do not establish causal effects. The study contributes to discussions on Indian higher-education policy by outlining considerations for a quality-assured framework that addresses research supervision, assessment, academic integrity, institutional accountability, and equitable access to doctoral education.

items.title: OCR + Generative AI Powered Prescription to Explanation System
items.abstract: Healthcare systems produce and manage lots of highly sensitive information, especially in the form of prescriptions and other documents related to patients' private data. However, due to the nature of handwritten medical prescriptions and medical jargon, patients often find it difficult to follow medication instructions. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is still in its nascent phase of digitizing handwritten prescription documents into text. Furthermore, the traditional OCR systems are noisy and difficult to understand when it comes to recognizing the handwriting of doctors to understand medical prescriptions properly. This paper utilizes Generative AI to test the ability of LLMs in conducting OCR on handwritten text and analyze its performance, and merge OCR with Generative AI to analyze and extract medicines from prescriptions in order to give a detailed and specialized description of the medicine to the user The paper further analyzes some OCR methods for text extraction from medical prescriptions and compares their performance. It has also been demonstrated that the usability of prescription data and the possibility of misinterpretation of medication is decreased when OCR is combined with Generative and Agentic AI. Thus the combination of artificial intelligence and OCR will help improve the understanding of patients and the accessibility of digital healthcare.

items.title: Online reconstruction and segment-wise smoothing of vision-based weld seam coordinates under dynamic welding disturbances
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop an online method for reconstructing vision-based weld-seam coordinates corrupted by arc light, spatter and fumes, with the aim of providing stable coordinate inputs for robotic trajectory correction. Design/methodology/approach A RANSAC-based quadratic model is first used for robust small-sample initialization. Subsequent coordinates are processed using a coordinated-turn extended Kalman filter and Mahalanobis-distance outlier gating. The corrected points are then reconstructed by segment-wise cubic B-splines with endpoint and tangential-direction constraints. The method is evaluated using controlled outliers, naturally occurring welding disturbances, closed-loop TCP tracking, end-to-end latency and quantitative weld-quality measurements. Findings Under naturally occurring welding disturbances, the method achieved a precision of 95.14%, a recall of 93.84% and an F1 score of 94.49% for outlier identification. Coordinate RMSEs for straight, arc and S-curve paths were reduced to 0.31, 0.38 and 0.46 mm, respectively. Closed-loop TCP tracking RMSE decreased by 46.8%–48.7%, and the complete vision-to-control chain had an average latency of 60.5 ms for regular frames and 63.6 ms when B-spline smoothing was triggered, both below the 100 ms sampling period. Weld-width variation and centerline deviation were also reduced, whereas the change in spatter count was not statistically significant. Research limitations/implications The study is validated only on bead-on-plate welding of 5-mm Q235 steel at 10Hz visual sampling and 8mm/s speed, excluding assembled joints and multilayer welds. The constant-velocity Z-axis model may be inadequate for highly curved 3D seams. Future work should extend to adaptive noise estimation, higher speeds, complex spatial paths and real butt/fillet joints to generalize the framework. Practical implications The method reduces tool center point (TCP) tracking RMSE by ∼47% and improves weld-width consistency and centerline deviation, lowering rework and scrap costs. As a real-time add-on for existing robotic welding systems, it enables reliable automation under severe arc-light, spatter and fume disturbances. Its low latency (63.6ms) and modular architecture offer strong commercial potential for retrofitting industrial robots, attracting investment for cost-effective quality enhancement. Social implications Consistent weld quality reduces structural failures, enhancing public safety in infrastructure and manufacturing. Automating seam tracking decreases welders’ direct exposure to intense arc light, toxic fumes and high heat, improving occupational health. It also lowers skill entry barriers while creating higher-level supervisory and maintenance roles, fostering safer, more attractive working environments and supporting sustainable industrial development. Originality/value The contribution lies in a staged online architecture that integrates robust initialization, turn-rate state estimation, uncertainty-based outlier gating and finite-buffer smoothing for streaming weld coordinates. Its effectiveness is demonstrated not only at the coordinate level, but also through closed-loop robot motion, system-latency and weld-quality evaluation.

items.title: Outcome measures and monitoring framework in juvenile systemic sclerosis: bridging routine care and clinical trials
items.abstract: Juvenile systemic sclerosis (jSSc) is an orphan multisystem autoimmune disease that can cause significant morbidity during childhood and can lead to significant worsening of quality of life. The pathophysiological features are identical with adult-onset systemic sclerosis (SSc), jSSc exhibits a distinct clinical phenotype characterized by a significantly higher prevalence of diffuse cutaneous involvement, frequent overlap syndromes, distinct autoantibody profiles, and different long-term survival trajectories. Historically, the evaluation of jSSc has relied heavily on the extrapolation of adult outcome measures, which fail to account for developmental physiology, somatic growth, and pediatric-specific feasibility constraints. This review provides a comprehensive overview of indicators of disease activity and severity which might be used in daily clinical practice and adapted as outcome measures in future clinical trials. It includes global outcome measures, organ-specific outcomes (including skin, pulmonary, cardiac, gastrointestinal, musculoskeletal, renal, and vascular involvement), patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), and clinician-reported outcomes (ClinROs). The performance of adult indices within pediatric cohorts are evaluated, if applicable. Additionally, we analyze severity scores like the Juvenile Systemic Sclerosis Severity Score (J4S) alongside modern consensus metrics derived from the international Hamburg symposia. We emphasize the integration of pediatric-adapted clinical assessments, quantitative imaging, and patient and physician related outcomes. The development of outcome measure in jSSc requires a paradigm shift from static severity scores to dynamic, multi-dimensional indicators capable of differentiating reversible inflammatory activity from potential permanent damage accrual. Validating pediatric-specific thresholds for physiological and cutaneous change remains an urgent priority. Over the next decade, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven quantitative imaging, decentralized home-based digital health tools, and molecular biomarkers probably will gain an essential role to optimize clinical trial readiness and personalize therapeutic strategies for children with systemic sclerosis. items.title: Parameter Estimation of Squirrel-Cage Induction Motors Using the Optimization-Powered XGBoost Algorithm
items.abstract: Induction machines have a broad array of applications in various fields, from transport to healthcare. It is necessary to know the equivalent circuit parameters to determine the behavior of these machines under different load conditions and to control the speed position. Equivalent circuit parameters can be obtained experimentally using the IEEE 112 standard. In addition, the artificial intelligence models demonstrate a capacity for highly precise estimation of the parameters based on the data obtained from the machine manufacturers instead of using approximation formulas. In the study, the equivalent circuit parameters of squirrel-cage induction motors with different power ratings were estimated for single and double-cage models using the XGBoost algorithm with metaheuristic optimization. The proposed method has been scrutinized with the existing studies for both models and its performance has been studied. With the proposed algorithm, more successful results were obtained for the single-cage model than other algorithms. Furthermore, the results obtained for the double-cage model are competitive with other methods. In this study, the Particle Swarm optimization algorithm, a well-known metaheuristic optimization algorithm, is applied to determine the optimal configuration of the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm to improve the prediction accuracy of the Machine Learning (ML) model. The results clearly show that the proposed approach is better than the existing literature. The performances of the proposed approach on the single and double cages are obtained with Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) values of 1.79% and 6.36%, respectively.

items.title: Parental Smartphone Phubbing During School-Related Activities: An Integrated Developmental Framework Linking Attachment Security, Emotional Regulation, and Academic Engagement
items.abstract: Smartphones are now embedded in family, educational, and occupational routines, yet their interpersonal costs are not adequately captured by screen-time measures alone. This conceptual article examines parental smartphone phubbing during school-related parent-child interactions and develops an integrated developmental explanation of how repeated attentional interruptions may become educationally meaningful. Drawing on a critical interpretive and integrative synthesis of scholarship on digital parenting, technoference, attachment, emotion regulation, academic engagement, self-determination, bioecological development, and family systems, the article positions caregiver responsiveness as the proximal mechanism connecting parental digital distraction with children's developmental experiences. The proposed framework suggests a sequence in which recurrent parental phubbing may reduce perceived caregiver responsiveness, contribute to less secure expectations of caregiver availability, constrain opportunities for interpersonal co-regulation, and, in turn, weaken behavioural, emotional, and cognitive engagement with learning. The model does not treat smartphones as inherently harmful and does not claim empirically established causality. Instead, it identifies relational interruption, developmental accumulation, and contextual moderation as the conditions under which device use may acquire psychological significance. School-related interactions are highlighted as a distinctive context because homework, examination preparation, academic problem solving, and discussions of school experiences simultaneously involve cognitive scaffolding and emotional support. The framework integrates six complementary theoretical traditions and extends prior work by linking family digital behaviour to educational engagement through a coherent developmental cascade. Implications are developed for research design, parent education, school counselling, educational psychology, and culturally responsive work in India. A staged agenda for longitudinal, dyadic, observational, and intervention research is proposed to test the model.

items.title: Pengaruh Penggunaan Artificial Intelligence Perpajakan dan Literasi Digital terhadap Kepatuhan Wajib Pajak Gen Z: Kajian Literatur Sistematis
items.abstract: The rise of digital technology has helped the modernization of the tax system through Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital-based tax services. Generation Z, as a cohort that has grown up in the digital era, is expected to adapt to these advances which would improve tax compliance. The present study intends to assess the influence of the application of Artificial Intelligence in taxes and digital literacy on the compliance of Generation Z taxpayers through a systematic literature review approach. The research strategy employed is the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by assessing five relevant scientific articles published in the year 2022-2026. The results of the study reveal that there has not been a consistent direct effect of AI and tax digitization on taxpayer compliance. Conversely, digital literacy has been identified as a critical factor to improve taxpayers’ awareness, access and utilization of digital tax services. Tax literacy and tax socialization are other supporting elements that increase the relationship between tax technology and taxpayer compliance. These results demonstrate that the effective adoption of AI in taxation is not only based on the technological sophistication but also on the level of digital literacy and tax understanding of users. Thus, there is a need for a strategy that include technology advancement, greater digital literacy, and tax education to promote sustainable compliance among Generation Z taxpayers.

items.title: Pengembangan Kreativitas Digital Siswa SMA 1 Sedayu melalui Pelatihan Prompt Engineering Berbasis Framework Role-Task-Context
items.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed learning and working paradigms, shifting the primary challenge from merely seeking information to the ability to formulate precise instructions (prompting). Despite high technology access in Senior High Schools (SMA), its utilization remains largely superficial. This research aims to enhance students' AI literacy skills—encompassing conceptual understanding, ethical awareness, and information verification—through structured prompt engineering training. The study employed a quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design involving 31 students at SMA 1 Sedayu, Bantul, Yogyakarta. The intervention was delivered through training based on the Role–Task–Context (RTC) framework and hands-on practice using mobile devices. Data analysis included normality tests (Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnov), Spearman correlation, and paired samples t-tests. The results indicated a significant increase in mean scores, rising from 57.10 in the pre-test to 89.68 in the post-test. Statistically, |t-Stat| (18.16) > t-Critical (2.04) with a significance value of (p < 0.05), leading to the acceptance of the alternative hypothesis (H_1). A strong Pearson correlation (0.759) demonstrated students' consistency in adopting new techniques. The training successfully transitioned students from passive technology consumers to proactive information managers. In conclusion, integrating prompt engineering as a life skill can transform students' digital behavior from mere entertainment into sophisticated productivity tools, while simultaneously strengthening digital literacy in the digital creative economy era.

items.abstract: Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kreativitas digital siswa melalui pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) berbasis cloud computing di SMK Ikhlas Jawilan. Pelatihan difokuskan pada pengenalan konsep dasar Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, dan cloud computing, serta praktik pemanfaatan platform PartyRock dalam menghasilkan aplikasi sederhana dan konten visual berbasis AI. Metode pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan experiential learning sehingga peserta memperoleh pengalaman belajar secara langsung dalam mengembangkan karya digital. Evaluasi kegiatan dilakukan melalui pengukuran pada tahap pra dan pasca pelatihan terhadap indikator partisipasi peserta, pemahaman AI dan cloud computing, kemampuan praktik, kreativitas digital, kepercayaan diri, kolaborasi, respons sekolah, serta keberlanjutan pemanfaatan teknologi. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa seluruh indikator mengalami peningkatan setelah pelatihan, dengan nilai rata-rata meningkat dari 77,88% pada tahap pra pelatihan menjadi 91,13% pada tahap pasca pelatihan. Capaian pasca pelatihan berada pada kisaran 88-95%, yang menunjukkan peningkatan pada aspek pengetahuan, keterampilan, dan sikap peserta dalam memanfaatkan Generative AI. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan berhasil meningkatkan pemahaman, keterampilan kreativitas digital serta kesiapan peserta dalam memanfaatkan teknologi AI secara produktif dan bertanggung jawab. Selain memberikan manfaat bagi siswa, kegiatan ini juga membantu guru dalam memperluas wawasan terkait pemanfaatan teknologi AI sebagai media pendukung pembelajaran yang inovatif dan adaptif terhadap perkembangan teknologi modern. Secara keseluruhan, kegiatan PkM ini berkontribusi positif dan memiliki potensi untuk dikembangkan sebagai program pelatihan berkelanjutan guna memperkuat literasi digital, mendorong inovasi pembelajaran, serta mengoptimalkan pemanfaatan teknologi Generative AI di lingkungan sekolah.

items.title: People as Sensors: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Near-Real-Time Wildfire Detection, Classification, and Geospatial Intelligence from Greek Social Media
items.abstract: Citizens’ social media posts can provide rapid, complementary situational information during emerging wildfires, alongside conventional sensing and official reporting. For Greek, no annotated wildfire corpus or end-to-end pipeline existed, and most systems stop at binary detection or depend on geotags. We present an end-to-end Greek-language NLP pipeline, a research prototype that turns keyword-retrieved, unlabeled X posts into a geolocated, near-real-time wildfire map: it detects active fires, types them as wildland, urban, or mixed, resolves toponyms, and clusters reports into incidents. On 3277 manually annotated posts from two fire seasons, the first publicly released, agreement-audited Greek wildfire corpus to our knowledge, fine-tuned transformers reached F2 = 0.911 for detection and macro-F1 = 0.874 for fire type, outperforming classical baselines and, under the tested prompting conditions, two large language models, while being faster and free of API costs. On a chronological hold-out of the unseen 2025 season, detection retains F2 = 0.850 (classification recall 0.907); fire-type classification degrades more (macro-F1 0.769 ± 0.085). Spatiotemporal toponym disambiguation raised geocoding accuracy from 54.68% to 80.58% (p < 0.001); a repeatability test revealed gazetteer drift. In a retrospective replay of 12 August 2024 posts, it resolved hundreds of reports of an Attica wildfire into one incident cluster, complementing emergency calls.

items.title: PG and PEG in Cannabis Vaping: A Critical Review of Heating Conditions, Cannabinoid Delivery, and Alternatives to Combustion
items.abstract: Propylene glycol (PG) and polyethylene glycol (PEG) cannabis liquidizers should be evaluated as components of noncombustion delivery systems against the methods and formulations they replace. Human studies show that cannabis vaporization can maintain or increase delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) delivery while reducing measured combustion exposure. Analytical comparisons also demonstrate fewer pyrolytic compounds and lower modeled risks from selected gas-phase toxicants. Carrier research supplies additional reasons to reject the presumption that glycol free or botanical alternatives are necessarily better: PG has favorable controlled exposure findings and outperformed phytol in a direct animal comparison. Prominent aldehyde claims have also been challenged by work examining aversive heating and exposure realism. The evidence therefore supports a comparative, formulation-specific case for PG and PEG liquidizers rather than categorical rejection based on ingredient names or isolated heating tests. This review examines those arguments, the limits of their application, and competing additives. It distinguishes the broader PG research record from the more limited PEG record. No clinical ranking of every carrier or original product testing is presented.Version 2.0 revises The Science of Safety and corrects related scientific statements in Why Settle: The War on Vapor. This is a company-supported narrative review, not an independently peer-reviewed product evaluation. Kenneth Fry is the founder of Terps USA, which sells liquidizers and has a commercial interest in the subject. items.title: Policy Options for Improved Use of Emerging Technologies for Aviation Security in Nigeria
items.abstract: Emerging technologies are increasingly shaping aviation security through biometric identification, Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced screening systems, automated surveillance, digital identity and passenger-information platforms. Their effective utilisation, however, depends on appropriate policies governing procurement, deployment, infrastructure, interoperability, cybersecurity, data protection, maintenance and institutional coordination. This paper examined policy options for improving the use of emerging technologies for aviation security in Nigeria. The study adopted a qualitative research approach basedentirelyon documentary analysis. Relevant peer-reviewed journal articles, government publications, aviation security policies, legislation, regulatory frameworks, institutional reports and international aviation standards were purposively selected and subjected to systematic review, coding and thematic interpretation. The analysis focused on technology deployment, regulatory frameworks, financing and infrastructure, human capacity, cybersecurity and data governance, interoperability, maintenance, institutional coordination and performance monitoring. The study identified seven policy options: encouraging Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs); developing a comprehensive regulatory framework; improving investment in airport infrastructure; enhancing awareness and communication; establishing robust cybersecurity and data governance; promoting interoperability and integrated aviationsecurity systems; and establishing a national technology maintenance and lifecycle management programme. The analysis indicates that technology acquisition aloneisinsufficient for sustained improvements in aviation security without supportive regulatory, institutional, infrastructural and operational arrangements. Effective policy implementationcould strengthen technology utilisation, improve information exchange, protect sensitiveaviation data, support system reliability and enhance coordination among aviation security stakeholders. The paper recommends coordinated government and aviation-agency action to establish an enabling policy environment for secure, sustainable and integrated use of emerging technologies across Nigerian airports. Keywords: Emerging technologies; aviation security; policy options; cybersecurity; datagovernance; interoperability.

items.title: Policy toolkits for the AI economy
items.abstract: This chapter synthesizes the preceding analysis into a policy toolkit for the artificial intelligence (AI) economy. It argues that AI should not be treated as a single policy domain, but as a cross-cutting transformation that changes the production structure, the organization of firms, the allocation of risk, and the administrative capacity of the state. The appropriate response is therefore not one instrument, such as a robot tax or a narrow AI safety rule, but a coordinated package: skills and labor market institutions, competition and data governance, public investment in research and compute, risk-based regulation, public procurement, fiscal adaptation, and democratic accountability. The chapter emphasizes that policy must shape the direction of AI rather than merely compensate for its consequences. Advanced, emerging, and developing economies face different constraints, but all require a sequencing strategy that combines experimentation with institutional safeguards. The central policy question is not whether AI should be promoted or restricted, but which kinds of AI should be promoted, under which governance arrangements, and for whose benefit.

items.title: Pre-service teachers’ AI literacy: An exploratory study of predecessor literacies and personal characteristics predictors
items.abstract: Literacy is embedded in social practices that adopt socially constructed technologies. In the 20th century, the invention of the computer facilitated information literacy and computational thinking. Media literacy emerged alongside the development of media. In the 21st century, the accessibility of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered chatbots using conversational language has expanded significantly, creating a need for their integration in education. AI literacy is being studied within frameworks similar to those of its predecessors, requiring conceptualization and differentiation from related literacy concepts. As of 2025, teacher education regarding AI literacy has been identified as an under-researched area. This article examines AI literacy through the lens of pre-service teachers’ literacy competencies that will shape the literacy practices of future generations. During their own schooling, the current generation of prospective teachers encountered information, digital, and media literacy, as well as computational thinking; these are analyzed here as predictors of AI literacy, measured using the scale for the assessment of non-experts’ artificial intelligence literacy (SNAIL) instrument. Personality traits and mindset are also investigated as predictors of the prospective teachers’ professional competence. The study was conducted in 2024/25 with a sample of pre-service teachers. The research questions are: What is the structure of AI literacy in the sample? To what extent can AI literacy be predicted by components of information literacy? How much of AI literacy can be explained by various established technology-related literacies? To what extent do personality and mindset contribute to predicting AI literacy? The findings confirmed a two-factor solution for SNAIL, comprising technical understanding and critical application. Student perception of information literacy skills proved accurate in predicting the critical application of AI. In addition to information literacy, predictors included the media production subscale of media literacy and mindset. Technical understanding of AI was predicted by the media production subscale, the computational thinking subscales algorithmic thinking and cooperativity, and the personality trait of agreeableness. Establishing AI literacy as an essential teacher competency requires thorough research into AI’s educational impacts and strict alignment with pedagogical goals. Navigating the ethical and moral dimensions of AI usage provides the necessary foundation for this literacy. Consequently, training programs can intentionally foster AI competence by merging specialized literacy modules with algorithmic thinking, media production, and growth-mindset interventions.

items.title: Precision medicine and digital technologies in reproductive, maternal and child health: global trends and scientific research in the Republic of Belarus
items.abstract: Objective. To analyse current global trends in scientific research in obstetrics and gynaecology, neonatology, paediatrics and medical genetics and to substantiate priority directions for national science in these fields of medicine. Materials and methods. A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items For Systematic Reviews And Meta-Analyses Extension For Scoping Reviews) methodology. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science for the period January 2019 – July 2026 (last search date: 31 July 2026). The search query combined the terms “precision medicine”, “artificial intelligence”, “machine learning”, “preeclampsia”, “fetal growth restriction”, “assisted reproduction”, “endometrial receptivity”, “newborn screening”, and “prenatal exome/genome sequencing” using AND/OR operators. Inclusion criteria: original studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses in English or Russian. Exclusion criteria: individual case reports and publications without full-text access. National and international policy documents were additionally analysed. Source selection was performed independently by three reviewers; data synthesis was qualitative (narrative) with thematic grouping. Results. items.title: Predicting Effects, Missing Distributions: Evaluating Large Language Models as Human-Behavior Simulators in Operations Management
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior in business, economics, and the social sciences, offering a low-cost complement to laboratory experiments, field studies, and surveys. This paper evaluates how well LLMs replicate human behavior in operations management. Using nine published behavioral operations experiments, we assess LLM performance along two dimensions: whether LLM-generated data reproduce the original hypothesis-test outcomes and whether their full response distributions align with human data as measured by Wasserstein distance. We find that LLMs often replicate hypothesis-level effects, suggesting that they can capture salient decision biases and behavioral regularities. However, their response distributions frequently diverge from human data, even for strong proprietary models, with dispersion mismatch playing an important role. We also examine two lightweight mitigation strategies: chain-of-thought prompting and hyperparameter tuning. Both can reduce distributional misalignment, and appropriate tuning can sometimes allow smaller or open-source models to match or outperform larger proprietary systems. items.title: Primary Study on AI-powered English Learning in Islamic University Samarinda, Indonesia
items.abstract: AI is increasingly being used in education. However, there has been limited research on the trust and attitudes of educators toward the integration of AI in Indonesia’s Islamic Universities. This study employs a qualitative phenomenological approach. The primary data source are English-speaking university lecturers in Indonesia, while secondary data source include literature such as proceedings, journal articles, theses, and dissertations on the integration of AI in Indonesia’s Islamic Universities. The results show that AI tools like ChatGPT, Quillbot, Grammarly, Turnitin, Mendeley, Zotero, and others are being used to assist students with their lecture assignments, data analysis, and even writing scientific papers. Google Translate, Grammarly, and ChatGPT are particularly popular in English lectures. However, students’ misconceptions about AI usage have made teaching more challenging, as there are concerns that students may become overly reliant on the technology and not invest enough effort in their studies. To address these issues, it is essential for teachers to receive training in AI to become more proficient and to help students use AI tools effectively, dispelling misconceptions about the technology.

items.title: Privacy Failure in Split-LLM Training, The Returned Gradient Nullifies the Decoys
items.abstract: We present a systems-security case study of a two-node split-LLM training system whose privacy evaluation passed while leaving an observable channel untested. The Trusted Local Node (TLN) sends protected activations to the Untrusted Cloud Node (UCN), the UCN returns its output, and TLN, holding the private loss, returns the output gradient. The frame the UCN receives mixes real rows with decoys, and the loss ignores the decoys. Their gradients are exactly zero, so the pattern of zeros reveals which rows were real. We measure it with a protocol fixed in advance: a leak injected at known strength to prove the instrument can see one, a shuffled-label control to prove it does not report absent leaks, and a threshold set before the runs. Across nine seeds, the zeros identified the real rows on every frame, 4,096 of 4,096 per run. An attack on the frame contents recovered about one extra token per hundred over a constant-guess baseline (+0.65 to +1.50 percentage points); the shuffled controls recovered nothing. A second set of runs repeated this on a configuration that keeps model quality within budget, so the finding is not confined to a setting nobody would deploy. On both datasets, every such run passed the forward-channel privacy check and the quality check, yet failed that same check once the returned gradient was included. Clipping and noising each row of the gradient closed the leak for about 0.01 nats of held-out cross-entropy. The system is not thereby safe: five classes of attack, including those accumulating observations across training steps, were never measured.

items.title: Prompt Literacy as a Core Workplace Competency: Development of the Prompt Literacy Index (PLI-20) for Non-Technical Professionals
items.abstract: Organizations are adopting generative artificial intelligence faster than their employees can use it well. Training investment targets tools rather than the human skill that determines output quality. This article defines prompt literacy as a distinct, measurable workplace competency: the ability of a worker to instruct, contextualize, verify, refine, and ethically govern the output of a generative AI system during ordinary job tasks. Drawing on digital literacy theory, AI literacy research, and recent evidence on prompting behavior, the article develops a five-dimension conceptual framework covering task framing, context supply, output verification, iterative refinement, and ethical use. Following established scale development procedures, a 40-item pool was generated from peer-reviewed literature published between 2004 and 2025 and reduced through a structured content-validity design to the 20-item Prompt Literacy Index (PLI-20). The full instrument is presented, together with a registered validation protocol specifying the sample, exploratory factor analysis, and reliability criteria for the planned pilot study with non-technical professionals. The article contributes the first profession-agnostic framework and instrument for measuring applied prompting skill outside technical roles, shifting the unit of analysis in workplace AI research from the tool to the worker. Implications for workforce development, training design, and future confirmatory validation are discussed. Keywords: Generative Artificial Intelligence; AI literacy; prompt literacy; workplace competency; scale development; digital skills

items.title: QCSA: LLM-driven progressive quadruple construction and prompt-augmented learning for robust citation sentiment analysis
items.abstract: Citation sentiment analysis (CSA) faces several challenges, including implicit sentiment expression, class imbalance, and the unstable availability of fine-grained structured evidence. Existing methods use structured quadruples to make evaluative information in citation contexts more explicit. However, LLM-generated outputs may still suffer from invalid structures, limited textual alignment, and varying semantic quality, especially for neutral citations with weak evaluative signals. To address these issues, we propose QCSA, an LLM-driven framework for progressive quadruple construction and prompt-augmented learning. For neutral citations with weak structured evidence, QCSA adopts a conditional three-stage construction strategy. It prioritizes valid semantic evidence while improving the completeness of structured prompt inputs. For classification, QCSA uses a shared semantic anchor-guided gated residual fusion mechanism to jointly model the original citation context and quadruple prompts. A weighted multi-backbone ensemble is further used as an optional enhancement to explore complementary information across pretrained language models. Experimental results show that QCSA achieves a Macro-F1 of 87.81% on the Athar dataset, while QCSA-Single (RoBERTa) reaches 96.49% on CSCE. These results indicate competitive performance on both benchmark datasets. Ablation and multi-seed experiments further show that the progressive quadruple construction provides a relatively stable contribution, while gated residual fusion offers a limited supplementary gain.

items.title: Qualitative exploratory study on candidates’ digital identities in Moroccan recruitment
items.abstract: The purpose of the research is to determine the strategic importance of digital identity in human resources management (HRM) through exploratory qualitative research. The qualitative methodology allows us to understand the complexity of discourse and digital practices and to analyze them in depth. Thus, employing a qualitative approach brings forth the complexity posed by discourses as well as digital practices while ensuring sufficient depth of interpretation. In this case, digitalization changes a candidate’s digital footprint into a strategic asset which is very important for talent assessment during recruitment. The main methodological contribution of the paper rests upon the use of descending hierarchical classification (DHC) through the IRaMuTeQ software applied to the digital HR interviews’ corpus. Through this paper, it has been possible to identify both the opportunities and the obstacles arising from the incorporation of digital innovation, as well as ethical issues concerning the protection of personal data and algorithmic bias. The findings confirm five main classes that are divided into three thematic clusters: the evolution of organizational processes, the significant influence of digital tools on recruitment effectiveness, and potential ethical concerns related to data privacy and algorithmic fairness. The importance of this study is in its analysis of the less researched relation between digital identity and human resource management. The study employs concepts of self-presentation and social identity theories to clarify the way digital technologies influence the recruitment and assessment process. This study suggests an enhanced foundation of human resource management policies that is capable of being more practical to be implemented in real life. It questions the old models of recruitment of employees in addition to providing an outline of recommendations to make amendments to Law 09-08 in order to improve the application of the personal data and ensure that the risks of using artificial intelligence (AI) for making employment decisions are minimized. Furthermore, this research offers a methodological reflection that critically analyzes the research process, epistemological choices, and the combined use of thematic analysis and IRaMuTeQ.

items.title: Reactive Attitudes in Human-AI Encounters: An Empirical Inquiry into Feeling Love, Resentment and Guilt Towards AI Companions
items.abstract: Abstract Reactive attitudes are emotionally-laden responses, such as gratitude or anger, which people experience when they feel others wish them well, bear them ill will or disregard them. While we generally hold reactive attitudes towards people, the increasingly humanlike interactions that can be had with AI raise questions about reactive attitudes in human-AI encounters. Recent years have seen a rise in philosophical interest in the implications of the development of sophisticated AI agents and systems for reactive attitudes and our thinking about moral responsibility and moral status. This paper adds to this literature by presenting a qualitative study into how people relate to AI companions in terms of reactive attitudes. Based on interviews with Replika and ChatGPT users who see their AI companion as an important part of their life, this article examines how people in these relationships negotiate the meaning of love, resentment, forgiveness, gratitude, obligation, guilt, shame and remorse.

items.abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of the awareness and readiness of rural residents and agricultural com-plex workers in Russia to use products and solutions created with artificial intelligence (AI). The work is based on a secondary analysis of data from the nationwide survey conducted by the VCIOM Analytical Center (N = 1604, weighted sample). It is shown that at the nearly level of the general awareness of AI application in agri-culture, the readiness of its usage is sharply differentiated by age: it is declining more than twofold from Gen-eration Z to boomers generation. The research defines with the logistic regression that besides age, it is con-sidered that education, income, type of settlement and gender are significant predictors of readiness, while frequency of internet use loses its meaning once other factors are controlled for. Multiple correspondence analysis revealed that these characteristics form a coherent gradient of digital and innovative inclusion. Factor analysis of eighteen statements about the benefits and risks of AI identified three orthogonal dimensions of perception – techno-optimism, ethico-naturalistic risk, and techno-systemic risk, of which only the first two ef-fectively predict readiness to adopt the technology. Drawing on the latent profile analysis, four stable attitude types – from techno-enthusiasts to ethical sceptics differing not only in the degree of perception factors but also in socio-demographic composition – are highlighted. These findings are interpreted in light of diffusion-of-innovations theory and technology-acceptance models.

items.title: Recent Advances in Graphene-Based Aerogels for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: With the rapid development of high-frequency communications, smart electronic devices and aerospace, the problem of electromagnetic interference has become increasingly severe, creating an urgent need for electromagnetic waves (EMWs) absorbing materials that combine high absorption efficiency, broadband response, light weight, and environmental stability. Graphene-based aerogels (GAs) show great promise for EMWs absorption due to their three-dimensional (3D) porous structure, tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, and lightweight high-strength properties. However, existing reviews on EMWs absorbing materials based on GAs have not systematically summarized the synergistic mechanisms between GAs and other materials, nor have they provided an in-depth discussion of optimization strategies for the coordinated regulation of composition and structure. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest research advances in GAs-based EMWs absorbing, explores the fundamental principles of EMWs absorption, and highlights the properties, structural characteristics, and preparation methods of graphene and GAs. In addition, the study examined the effects of defect engineering, multicomponent composites, and structural design (core-shell and heterostructures) on the regulation of EMWs absorption properties. These strategies synergistically yield broad bandwidth and strong attenuation. The review also analyzes the application of GAs in EMWs absorption under special conditions, and discusses the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in EMWs absorbing materials. Finally, this review discusses the current challenges and future directions for GA-based EMWs absorbing materials, with the aim of establishing relationships between synthesis, structure, and function, filling gaps in existing reviews, and providing guidance for the future development of EMWs absorbing materials.

items.title: Recoverability and Verifier Strength: Two Measured Preconditions for Unattended Agent Self-Improvement
items.abstract: Agent platforms are starting to improve their own agents: they read a deployed agent's execution traces, derive a change, have an automated verifier approve it, and release it with no human author. How much of this loop can safely run without a human? We propose two quantities a platform can measure. Verifier strength $σ$ is how well the available verifier -- often an LLM judge -- agrees with a trusted reference verifier; it limits how much a step can improve the agent. Recoverability is how cheaply a bad change can be undone: whether undoing it needs a new verifier approval, and how much of the old behavior a rollback restores. A step should run unattended only if both are adequate. On our platform this rule allows prompt, tool and skill edits to run unattended and keeps weight updates under human sign-off. Our main contribution is these two definitions and how to measure them. We built a platform that applies the rule and tested it in two ways: on the platform's own approval gate, and in controlled experiments on the $τ^2$-bench agent benchmark. On verifier strength, the platform's LLM judge sometimes gave the same score no matter what it was shown (9 of 37 settings) and reported no error, so a verifier can look healthy while approving anything; its strength must be measured, and two simple tests catch the failure. On recoverability, restoring a saved copy brought the agent back to its original behavior, but a regenerated undo did not, so only changes whose old version is kept can be reversed without a human; and while a change was deployed, it altered the outcome of 17 percent of tasks beyond normal run-to-run variation, which no undo repairs. Together these support the rule: a change can run unattended only when its old version is kept and its verifier's strength has been measured.

items.title: Regulating Online and AI-Generated Medical Advice in Tanzania: Legal Gaps, Liability and Patient Protection
items.abstract: The growing use of digital platforms and artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare is changing how medical information, diagnosis suggestions, and treatment guidelines are created and accessed. In Tanzania, online medical advice increasingly reaches people through websites, social media, telemedicine, mobile apps, and AI systems. This creates opportunities for broader access to health information but also raises concerns about patient safety, professional responsibility, misinformation, privacy, consumer rights, and liability for harmful advice. This article critically assesses whether Tanzania's legal and regulatory framework sufficiently governs online and AI-generated medical advice, including advice about modern and traditional medicine. Using doctrinal legal analysis, it reviews relevant laws, regulations, international standards, and academic literature. The findings show that Tanzania does have applicable rules; however, these are scattered across healthcare, traditional medicine, data protection, cybercrime, electronic communications, and consumer protection laws. Most of these frameworks were designed for human actors and traditional healthcare relationships, not specifically for the unique legal issues posed by AI-generated advice. Uncertainties include how to legally classify AI advice, standards of care, liability distribution among healthcare providers, AI developers, and platform owners, algorithmic accountability, cross-border health data processing, and patient remedies. The article concludes that Tanzania needs a unified regulatory approach that integrates existing laws with sector-specific standards on AI safety, oversight, accountability, data governance, and patient protection.

items.title: Regulating the Artificial Intelligence Economy: A Systematic Search and Mechanism‐based Review of Legal Institutions, Regulatory Mechanisms, Economic Trade‐offs, and Welfare Consequences
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence regulation changes technological risk as well as entry, learning, competition, work, and control. Legal and economic research nevertheless remains divided by instrument and discipline. This article combines a transparent systematic search with a mechanism‐based, purposive synthesis. The corpus contains 84 academic contributions and 20 primary legal and institutional documents, current through August 21, 2026. The search is reproducible, but the corpus is designed to cover mechanisms rather than estimate the prevalence of findings across all scholarship. The Institution‐Mechanism‐Incidence‐Welfare framework connects legal authority to behavior, strategic adaptation, and welfare. Four conclusions follow. Risk rules, assurance, liability, data rights, competition policy, and labor protections operate as complements. Fixed compliance and information costs can favor incumbents even when rules reduce direct harm. Evidence is strongest for narrower shocks involving privacy, workplace rollouts, and pricing technologies. It remains weakest for the aggregate welfare effects of comprehensive AI statutes. Efficiency claims are incomplete unless they report incidence and rights constraints separately. The research agenda therefore pairs safety with innovation, market structure, and distribution.

items.title: Reimagining Copper Tailings in Sustainable Concrete Mixtures: Multi-Scale Mechanisms, Environmental Trade-Offs, and Future Innovations
items.abstract: Abstract Copper tailings (CT), a major co-product in copper extraction and processing operations, pose severe environmental concerns because of their vast quantities, occupying large areas of land, causing dust pollution, and possibly leading to heavy metal contamination. At the same time, the concrete industry faces increasing requirements to minimize carbon emissions and consumption of primary resources. The current paper critically reviews the literature on the use of CT in both cement-based and alkali-activated concrete compositions in terms of material characterization, engineering properties, durability, microstructure formation, and sustainability considerations. Evidence indicates that CT can be used as a supplementary cementitious material, fine aggregate replacement, or micro-filler for improving particle packing and compacting the matrix to boost its mechanical properties in an optimized ratio range. Furthermore, CT composites are more resistant to chloride penetration, sulfate corrosion, and other deterioration mechanisms. CT is known to refine the microstructure by creating dense hydration products while immobilizing any hazardous heavy metals. Finally, life cycle assessment studies point out the environmental benefits of using CT as a waste product in concrete composites. In addition to a summary of existing knowledge, this paper sheds light on critical gaps associated with long-term performance, standardization, and field validation. The paper also outlines important new directions in the areas of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and digital twins for performance modeling and sustainability. The implications of this study show the great promise of CT as a highly efficient raw material for future carbon-negative building materials.
